title: One protocol, two eras
brief: Hosts and servers in your estate sit on different MCP revisions, and a plain load balancer fronts the servers. You must decide which era to build for and how old and new peers connect. The client mix, the fleet shape and any need for server-initiated requests are open.

blocks.text: From a handshake to per-request metadata

blocks.caption: Revision timeline. Revisions are dated by the last backwards-incompatible change [[r1]]
head: Revision
What it added or changed
Status on 2026-10-13
rows: stdio and HTTP+SSE transports. MCP was open-sourced on 2024-11-25
OAuth 2.1 authorization framework, Streamable HTTP replaces HTTP+SSE, JSON-RPC batching, tool annotations, audio content [[r33]]

Batching removed. Structured tool output, servers classified as OAuth resource servers, RFC 8707 resource indicators required of clients, elicitation, resource links, `MCP-Protocol-Version` header [[r32]]
Client ID Metadata Documents, URL mode elicitation, experimental Tasks, JSON Schema 2020-12 default, OpenID Connect Discovery, SSE polling [[r31]]
Past revision, the last stateful one
Stateless model, `server/discover`, Multi Round-Trip Requests, `subscriptions/listen`, caching fields, Tasks as an extension [[r1]]

blocks.title: 2025-11-25: stateful lifecycle
blocks.alt: A client sends initialize, the server replies with capabilities and a session id, the client sends the initialized notification, then calls a tool with the session id header. The server later pushes an elicitation request on a stream.
blocks.src:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant S as Server
  C->>S: initialize with version and capabilities
  S-->>C: result and Mcp-Session-Id
  C->>S: notifications/initialized
  C->>S: tools/call with Mcp-Session-Id
  S-->>C: elicitation/create pushed on a stream
  C->>S: elicitation answer
blocks.caption: Version and capabilities are negotiated once. A server that assigns a session id expects it on every later request, answers 404 when the session is gone, and the client must then start over [[r21]] [[r22]].

blocks.title: 2026-07-28: stateless exchange
blocks.alt: A client optionally calls server discover. It then calls a tool with version and capabilities in metadata. The server returns input required with a request state, the client retries with input responses and gets a complete result.
blocks.src:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant S as Server
  C->>S: server/discover (optional)
  S-->>C: versions, capabilities, ttlMs
  C->>S: tools/call with _meta version and capabilities
  S-->>C: input_required and requestState
  C->>S: retry with inputResponses and requestState
  S-->>C: result with resultType complete
blocks.caption: Each request stands alone, so any instance behind a plain load balancer can answer it [[r1]] [[r3]].
What changed on the wire [[r1]] [[r2]] [[r21]] [[r22]]
head: Concern
2025-11-25 (stateful)
2026-07-28 (stateless)
rows: No handshake. `server/discover` is mandatory for servers and optional for clients
Sent in `_meta` on every request: `io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion` and `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities`
`Mcp-Session-Id` assigned at init. 404 means start a new session. DELETE ends it
No sessions and no header. Cross-call state uses explicit handles
Multi Round-Trip Requests: `input_required`, then a retry with `inputResponses`
Removed. A broken stream loses the request and the client re-issues it with a new id
`ttlMs` and `cacheScope` required. Deterministic `tools/list` order is a SHOULD
Resource not found is `-32602`. `UnsupportedProtocolVersionError` is `-32022`. `-32020` to `-32099` is reserved for MCP

blocks.title: Which era should a server target?
blocks.prompt: Flip the client mix, the fleet shape and the need for server-initiated sampling or roots.

values.label: A mix of old and new
One instance, sticky routing is fine
Autoscaled fleet behind a plain load balancer

dials.label: Server-initiated sampling or roots needed today

options.name: Stay on 2025-11-25
options.summary: Keep the initialize handshake and sessions.

options.name: Dual-era server
options.summary: Serve modern requests statelessly and legacy clients through initialize.

options.name: Modern only (2026-07-28)
options.summary: Drop sessions and the handshake entirely.

modern.why: A modern client against a legacy server fails. On stdio it should probe first so it fails deterministically.

single.why: One instance can hold session state in memory.

lb.why: Sessions need sticky routing or shared session storage.

yes.why: Server-initiated requests still work in the legacy era, though sampling is Deprecated.

modern.why: Works, but you carry a legacy path nobody uses.

mixed.why: A dual-era server serves both kinds of client. A request with modern `_meta` is stateless and an `initialize` selects legacy semantics.

legacy.why: Serves legacy clients and avoids the failure when they meet a modern-only server.

lb.why: The modern path is stateless, but the legacy path still needs stickiness or shared state.

yes.why: Legacy clients keep server-initiated requests. Modern clients get them through MRTR.

modern.why: Simplest code path and no legacy baggage.

mixed.why: Legacy clients get a 400 with no fall-forward mechanism.

single.why: Simple, though statelessness is not needed here.

lb.why: No sessions, no sticky routing and no shared session store.

no.why: Nothing blocks a clean stateless design.

yes.why: Sampling is Deprecated and only reachable through MRTR. Plan the move to direct model APIs.

blocks.takeaway: Statelessness pays when you scale out. Compatibility pays when the host mix is old. A dual-era server buys time at the price of two code paths.

blocks.md: Deprecated means the feature stays in the spec and keeps working. New work should not adopt it. A deprecated feature stays at least twelve months, or at least ninety days when removal is expedited for an active security risk [[r25]]. Elicitation is **not** deprecated. Tasks moved to an extension but are not deprecated. Agent Framework's docs say sampling removal comes no later than 2027-07-28, which is stricter than the spec's earliest-removal wording [[r26]].

items: **stdio**: newline-delimited JSON-RPC with no embedded newlines. A server MUST NOT write anything but MCP messages to stdout. stderr is free for logs and clients SHOULD NOT treat it as an error signal [[r2]].

**Streamable HTTP, 2026-07-28**: one endpoint. Every JSON-RPC message is its own POST with `Accept` listing `application/json` and `text/event-stream`. The reply is one JSON object or a per-request SSE stream. The GET stream and DELETE are gone. Servers MUST validate `Origin` (403 if invalid) and SHOULD bind local servers to 127.0.0.1 [[r2]].

**Required request headers, 2026-07-28**: `MCP-Protocol-Version` on every request, `Mcp-Method` on all requests, `Mcp-Name` for `tools/call`, `resources/read` and `prompts/get`. A mismatch with the body returns `HeaderMismatch` (`-32020`) [[r2]].
**Streamable HTTP, 2025-11-25**: one endpoint with POST and GET. A session id is returned at initialization. SSE event ids support resumption through `Last-Event-ID` [[r22]].
**HTTP+SSE**: the 2024-11-05 transport with separate `/sse` and `/messages` endpoints. Deprecated. Older tutorials still show it [[r9]].

blocks.caption: Expected outcome for each client and server era [[r24]]
head: Client
Server
Outcome
rows: Works. `server/discover` is optional. A version mismatch returns `UnsupportedProtocolVersionError` and the client retries with a shared version
Fails. On stdio the client SHOULD send `server/discover` first so it fails deterministically
Works. The client falls back to `initialize` after a non-modern error, a 4xx without a modern error body, or a timeout
Fails. Legacy clients have no fall-forward mechanism and get a 400 on HTTP
Works. The server answers `initialize` and serves the negotiated legacy revision

blocks.md: A modern-only server that receives an `initialize` request SHOULD name its supported versions in the error text, because that message may be the only diagnostic a legacy client can show. Clients SHOULD cache the detected era per server process on stdio or per origin on HTTP [[r24]].

blocks.title: Failure modes and how to detect them

items.symptom: Legacy hosts get HTTP 400 after a server upgrade
items.cause: A modern-only server rejects requests that lack the modern `_meta` and headers
items.fix: Run dual-era until a per-version request counter shows no legacy traffic. Name supported versions in the `initialize` error text

items.symptom: Intermittent 404 on legacy clients after scaling out, none on modern clients
items.cause: The legacy session lives on one instance and the load balancer is not sticky
items.fix: Use sticky routing or shared session storage for the legacy path, and move state into explicit handles for the modern path

items.symptom: A new client hangs against an old stdio server
items.cause: The client skipped the `server/discover` probe and waited for a modern reply
items.fix: Probe first on stdio, treat a non-modern error as legacy, and cache the era per process

items.symptom: One user reads or edits another user's basket
items.cause: A state handle was treated as a capability and not checked against the caller
items.fix: Authorize the handle against the verified user on every call. Use high-entropy, expiring handles for unauthenticated servers [[r6]]

items.symptom: A dropped stream reruns a non-idempotent tool
items.cause: Resumption is gone in 2026-07-28, so the client re-issues the request with a new id
items.fix: Pass idempotency keys, and use Tasks for calls that outlive a connection

quiz.q: Put the 2025-11-25 stateful startup and first call in order.
items: Client sends `initialize` with its protocol version and capabilities
Server replies with its capabilities and, over HTTP, an `Mcp-Session-Id`
Client calls `tools/list` and includes the session id on the request
quiz.explain: Initialization must be the first interaction. The server's reply carries its capabilities and the optional session id. The client confirms with the initialized notification and then operates, repeating the session id on every later HTTP request.

quiz.q: Select everything the 2026-07-28 revision removed or replaced.
quiz.explain: The handshake, protocol sessions with their header, and SSE resumption were removed. Elicitation stays active and rides on Multi Round-Trip Requests. `tools/call` is a core request that gained `resultType` and the option to return `input_required`.

quiz.q: A server must serve both new and old hosts and runs on an autoscaled fleet behind a plain load balancer. It does not need sampling. Which option fits?
options: Stay on 2025-11-25 and add sticky routing everywhere
Modern only, because it is the Current revision and every legacy client is expected to upgrade soon
Dual-era: stateless for modern requests, `initialize` for legacy ones
Drop Streamable HTTP and move to HTTP+SSE
quiz.explain: A mixed client base rules out modern-only, because legacy clients get a 400 with no fall-forward. Staying legacy blocks modern clients and forces sticky or shared sessions. HTTP+SSE is Deprecated. Dual-era keeps both reachable and keeps the modern path stateless.

quiz.q: Which statement about the deprecations in 2026-07-28 is correct?
options: Roots, Sampling and Logging are Deprecated but still functional, with earliest removal in the first revision released on or after 2027-07-28
Roots, Sampling and Logging were removed on 2026-07-28 and must be deleted from servers
Elicitation was deprecated together with Sampling because both ask the client for input
Dynamic Client Registration is the preferred registration method and HTTP+SSE is Current
quiz.explain: Deprecated features remain in the spec and keep working until a later revision removes them. Elicitation is not deprecated. Dynamic Client Registration is deprecated in favor of Client ID Metadata Documents, and HTTP+SSE was replaced by Streamable HTTP.

takeaways: 2026-07-28 replaced the handshake and session id with per-request `_meta`, a required `server/discover` and explicit handles.
Server-initiated requests became Multi Round-Trip Requests, and SSE resumption was removed.
Roots, Sampling, Logging, Dynamic Client Registration, HTTP+SSE and two `includeContext` values are Deprecated. Nothing is Removed yet.
Choose legacy, dual-era or modern by client mix and fleet shape. A modern client against a legacy-only server fails.
